description.narrative:
Description of the crisis (including the number of people affected, timeline, number of people reached by Oxfam to date, etc.):
The Central Sahel region (Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso and Chad), one of the most fragile in the world, is facing a most complex and pernicious humanitarian situation because it has been experiencing complex and multifaceted crises for decades, accentuated since 2012 by a climate of insecurity and violence due to the abuses of the GANES. The latter is suffering shocks that are both natural and anthropogenic, marked by armed conflicts, climatic, biological (attacks by crop pests, epidemics/epizootics), socio-economic shocks (inflation and rising commodity prices, terms of trade unfavourable to livestock farmers) and political shocks (stench of ECOWAS and UEOMA sanctions in Niger following the coup d'état). This deleterious situation contributes to reinforcing social inequalities, to experiencing good living together through marginalization, stigmatization and repeated violations of the human rights of certain communities. Despite this deplorable humanitarian context, Humanitarian Response plans are increasingly underfunded, regularly leaving human beings in a pernicious inability to meet their basic needs. The region is also facing a large-scale protection crisis in which women and children are disproportionately targeted, and rates of gender-based violence remain extremely high. As an indication, betweenNovember 2022 and October 2023, nearly 3,708 violent incidents were reported in the region. Also, the growing number of displaced persons and refugees (3,732,000 people for the 4 countries in October 2023) testifies to the deterioration of the situation with moreand more people in need of urgent humanitarian assistance. The growing influx of people forced to move to more secure areas, resulting in the overexploitation of basic socio-economic services and natural resources, is fuelling inter-community tensions. This year,this region is experiencing an unprecedented food crisis linked to a significant deficit in agrosilvopastoral production, which hasbeen added to the situation described above. As a result, the March 2024 Cadre Harmonisé (CH 2024) forecasts 9,640,842 people in crisis (IPC-3) and 840,088 people in emergency (IPC-4) in the June-August 2024 forecast. By March 2024, these targeted countries in the Central Sahel will collectively register more than 3 million displaced people within them, 8 times more than five years ago. In addition, they host nearly 1.2 million refugees and asylum seekers (FSNWG, May 2024). According to the Food Security and Nutrition Working Group's (FSNWG) alert note on West and Central Africa, May 2024, several countries in the Central Sahel are expected to have more than 10% of their population analysed in a crisis situation or worse in June-August 2024. These are Burkina Faso (2,734,196, 12 per cent), Niger (3,436,892, 13 per cent) and Chad (3,364,453, 20 per cent). In addition, the already difficult nutritional situation of communities in the region is deteriorating, as is their access to water, hygiene and sanitation. According to OCHA, in the Sahel region, 7,800 cases of cholera were recorded in 2023, with more than 200 associated deaths. This testifies, if need be, to the consumption by households of water from unimproved sources. This situation is all the more worrying as the sabotage of basic social service infrastructures by Non-State Armed Groups deprives more and more populations of access to basic social services, including access to water, not to mention the extortion of their property (livestock, food) by the same actors. The Central Sahel also remains one of the regions most affected by the effects of climate change, while, paradoxically, this area produces the least greenhouse gases. With a 40% increase in natural disasters expected by 2030, it is easy to conclude that the vulnerability of communities would increase by a significant amount that exceeds the endogenous capacity to respond. It should be noted that in 2023, Niger and Burkina Faso experienced severe floods that carried large areas of rainfed crops as well as rainfall breaks that were harmful to their proper development. This has also contributed to the above-mentioned deficit in agrosilvopastoral production. We must also add heat waves observed during the dry season production period, which also had a negative impact on some harvests. In view of all these challenges, Oxfam's 4 Country Directors in the Central Sahel (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Chad) have submitted a request within the Confederation (IO) to categorize this crisis of regional proportions. To do this, we must support these countries to enable them to have or maintain a fairly solid humanitarian structure in order to give them more operational capacities that can guarantee a consequent mobilization of resources to meet the growing humanitarian needs. This explains this request from the catfund for the 3 countries (Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger), Chad having already benefited from a grant in this direction a few months ago.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novibs main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fund raising, campaigning and advocacy. The Hub Niamey Niger exists since 2006 as a humanitarian field office and since 2012 as the decentralized Country office for Oxfam Novib, dealing with all the development and humanitarian themes like Sustainable livelihoods, Right to Basic services, Humanitarian and resilience interventions, The right to be heard and the right to an Identity, including women's rights and sexual and reproductive health rights. The Country Office in Niger works with local partners to realize the vision of a Niger without poverty
